Stage 02Reference Norm
RATING-CONDITIONED

◎ Build the MIRROR reference population

Import many PGN files containing WhiteElo/BlackElo (or equivalent rating headers). Every move is passed through the same P1 → P2 → P3 detector pipeline, perspective-normalized to the player who made the move. The database stores aggregated player/rating statistics, not raw games.

Reference Database
v5 · Rating-conditioned Neural
Rated contributors0
Rated player-sides0
Rated moves0
Rating bands0
The reference norm is built from the same Deep Atlas candidate pipeline as player analysis for every rated move, then trains a separate rating-conditioned population neural network from those actual-vs-viable-alternative decisions. The ~60-position Stockfish calibration layer is not rerun for the reference corpus. 100-Elo bands use smooth ±300 Elo weighting, and each player/rating contributor remains one statistical unit.

Stage 03Style Fingerprint
LIVE PROFILE

◈ Style Profile Transfer

Export the learned MIRROR style package from an analysed profile, then import it into another compatible MIRROR build. No PGNs or raw game history are included; the package carries the learned style state, semantic network, atlas statistics, repertoire memory, and calibrated profile data.

Model NotesHow MIRROR reads the evidenceREVEAL ⌄
Each detector tracks occurrence, opportunity and choice independently. An opportunity is position-level: at least one legal move satisfies the same detector. Objective nonsense is filtered softly rather than by popularity; unusual but playable choices stay in the sample. A player's own poor move is not a decline, and reliability is kept separate from the fingerprint score.

Stage 04Play the style bot
Match Setup
Rapid
Strength: —
100%100%
Targets the player's current Chess.com rating for the selected time control. Fidelity controls how strongly the learned player style is allowed to influence Maia/Stockfish. Sampling controls how sharply the displayed final probabilities are sampled. Adaptive style weighting uses Stockfish WDL expected-score loss first (with CP as a secondary fallback) so style has more freedom among engine-equivalent moves and less freedom when the engine sees a meaningful difference; its smooth curve is learned from independent held-out player decisions in the background. Auto starts at neutral 100% so the first move is never blocked by calibration, then builds cached held-out probability snapshots in the background and applies the calibrated temperature once enough independent cases are ready; uncheck Auto to set it manually. 100% uses the displayed probabilities directly.
